FAQ and troubleshooting

Source: vignettes/articles/faq.Rmd
faq.Rmd

Short answers to the questions that come up most often. If something here does not cover your case, please open an issue at https://github.com/lucp12891/MosaiClusteR/issues.

Installing and loading

Do I need a compiler? The M-ABC family ships C++ kernels, so building from source needs a C/C++ toolchain: Rtools on Windows, the Xcode command-line tools on macOS. The CRAN binaries already include the compiled code, so install.packages("MosaiClusteR") needs no toolchain. Every method also has a pure-R path, so the package still loads if a kernel is unavailable.

A method says a package is “required here”. Heavier and specialised methods declare their dependencies under Suggests and load them only when called. The message names the exact install command, for example install.packages("SNFtool") or BiocManager::install("MLP"). Install the named package and run the call again.

could not find function "M_ABCpp". The function was renamed to M_ABC() in 0.1.4. Update M_ABCpp(...) to M_ABC(...); the arguments and behaviour are unchanged.

Data shape and alignment

Which way round do my matrices go? Objects (samples) in rows, features in columns, for every source and every method, including the M-ABC family. This is the single most common mistake. If a result looks wrong or an example compresses the wrong dimension, check that you did not transpose a source.

# right: 60 objects in rows, 120 features in columns
dim(mosaic_toy$List[[1]])   #> 60 120

“the sources do not describe the same objects” (or a subscript error on older versions). Integration needs every source to cover the same objects. MosaiClusteR aligns the sources by row name and reports clearly when they do not match: different object sets, different row counts, or duplicated identifiers. Give each source row names, and make sure the sets agree. Reordered rows are fine; they are realigned for you.

My samples are not all measured in every source. Use NEMO(). It is the one method here that handles samples missing a modality, by averaging affinities over the omics that measured each pair, with no imputation. The other methods need the same objects across all sources.

Reproducibility

I get a different answer each run. Several methods are stochastic: the M-ABC family, ADEC(), intNMF(), and any step that uses k-means initialisation (spectral_clustering(), NEMO(), HBGF()). Fix the result with the method’s seed = argument where it has one, or with set.seed() before the call.

set.seed(1)
M_ABC(mosaic_toy$List, NC = 3, seed = 1)   # seed = also fixes it directly

Choosing the number of clusters

SelectnrClusters() returns a table, not a number. It gives one recommendation per criterion (a one-row data frame). Reduce it to a single integer, for example by taking the most frequent recommendation, before using it as a cluster count.

sel  <- SelectnrClusters(DistM, maxK = 8)
recs <- as.integer(unlist(sel$Optimal_Nr_of_CLusters))
k    <- as.integer(names(sort(table(recs), decreasing = TRUE))[1])

How do I read an agreement score? For cluster_agreement() ARI: above 0.90 excellent, 0.75 to 0.90 good, 0.50 to 0.75 moderate, below 0.50 weak. ARI, NMI and Jaccard all return 1 for identical partitions (up to relabelling), including the single-cluster and all-singleton cases.

Methods that need external tools

METIS or MATLAB. A few methods use an external graph-partitioning executable: EnsembleClustering(), the METIS path of EHC(), and LinkBasedClustering(linkBasedMethod = "asrs") (MATLAB). They raise an informative error when the tool is absent. Pure-R alternatives cover the same need: HBGF(), EvidenceAccumulation(), and the CTS or SRS paths of LinkBasedClustering().

Omics interpretation

Pathway and gene-set functions need Bioconductor. DiffGenes(), PathwayAnalysis(), Pathways() and the related functions use Bioconductor packages (limma, MLP, biomaRt, org.Hs.eg.db). Install them with BiocManager::install(...) as the error message names.

Performance

M-ABC is slow on my data. Runtime grows with the number of simulations (numsim), the number of sources, and the sample size. Start with a modest numsim, and for large N or heavy-tailed data use weighting = "nugget", which derives feature weights from a compact set of representatives rather than from every observation.
